brief:
The Quincy Institute has raised concerns about the efficacy of existing accountability frameworks in addressing actions taken during the Gaza conflict. The examination focuses on how elite actors face consequences through international and domestic legal systems.

The institute's analysis suggests significant gaps in current mechanisms designed to hold decision-makers responsible for conduct in Gaza, according to reporting on the topic. Questions persist about whether available tools adequately address violations or whether structural limitations prevent meaningful accountability.
title: Think tank questions accountability mechanisms for Gaza actions
